prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: Been a weekend of delays with , #roundtripdelays #notevenholidaytrafficyet
Delta: Hi, Eddie! Thanks for reaching out and sharing your concern. We certainly do everything possible to get our flights out on time, and we're sorry that this hasn't been the case for you lately today.  *TJN

Customer: Brandon is on top of customer service, flight 0834! Kudos to the awesome crew!
Delta: Happy to hear that. Thanks for sharing the compliment. 😊 *AMV

Customer: Thanks for the great service on our flight  ✈️👍🏽 Papa and I are very happy #DL1415 #MiamiBound  https://t.co/HxjA6j6mr4
Delta: Hey, we're glad you both are enjoying your flight! 😍😍 *AJY

Customer: Great weekend in TX. Ready to get back home and back on the air. Now the only issue is getting in the air.  already delayed my flight
Delta: I show that your flight is delayed due to air traffic control and is estimated to depart at 10:35am.  *HPL

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: rebooking_change):
"""“customer service” - Flight to GFK for next weekend, & charged me $300 to come home this weekend instead 4 dad’s ER open❤️surgery"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: We’re sorry to hear about the inconvenience. Please DM us with your reservation info so we can look into your re‑booking and the charge. Thank you.
